source_name: Celní správa ČR (Customs Administration) procurement documents — payment terminal operation contracts
why_relevant: Concrete worked example found in search: a competitive-dialogue protocol for 'Realizace provozu platebních terminálů pro CS ČR' involving ČSOB, published as a PDF on the authority's own site (VVZ form F2017-017645). Demonstrates the pattern that authority websites carry negotiation-stage documents naming the banks/acquirers involved — evidence TED alone never shows. Useful both as a source and as a template for finding equivalents at other authorities.

source_name: Zlatá koruna – financial product awards (Finanční akademie)
why_relevant: Named in the cell brief. Long-running (23rd edition) product-level award judged by a ~350-member Finanční akademie across ~24 categories, under Ministry of Finance and ČNB patronage. Category-level winners (e.g. MONETA Smart Banka as banking product of the year, Česká spořitelna in Payment cards / Online applications) identify which digital implementations the market rates — a direct feed into case-study discovery. The canonical award domain was not confirmed in this pass, so the reachable entry point is the press-release cluster.

source_name: Visa Awards CZ – annual Czech payments awards (press coverage cluster)
why_relevant: Visa's CZ awards ceremony (Signal Space gallery, Prague) hands out category prizes that read as a market share and implementation map: Partners Banka for best Visa-as-a-Service implementation, wFlow for New Flows, Raiffeisenbank #1 Issuer, Global Payments #1 Acquirer, plus Fio, KB, Česká spořitelna, mBank. Extremely dense partnership/vendor signal; only reachable via the press-release cluster since no standalone award site was found.

source_name: Finparáda – Finanční produkty roku
why_relevant: A third, methodologically distinct CZ product award (run by the Finparáda comparison site) covering savings, accounts, loans and investments. Its rankings are a useful triangulation against Zlatá koruna and Banka roku, and its category set changes with market fashion (a leading indicator of product-area competition).

source_name: ČBA — schéma okamžitých plateb / standardy a dokumenty ke stažení
why_relevant: ČBA publishes the rulebooks and standards for national payment schemes (okamžité platby / instant payments, API standards for open banking). These documents name participating institutions, scheme roles and technical requirements — direct evidence of what vendors must build to and who has joined.

source_name: Cvak A2A payment rollout coverage (Albert, Lidl) – Měšec.cz / HN / Deník
why_relevant: Highest-value current buy-side signal: major grocery chains (Albert first, then Lidl CZ across ~326 stores) adopting Cvak account-to-account payments — backed notably by Air Bank, with Fio, mBank and Moneta clients supported — explicitly to cut card-scheme fees and as a fallback during card outages. Direct evidence of card-rail disintermediation driven by merchant economics.

source_name: Temenos success story: Komerční banka
why_relevant: Named CZ core-banking win: KB on Temenos Core + Data Hub since 2021, phased retail migration to 2025, private cloud on Kubernetes/PostgreSQL, LTIMindtree as SI. Dates, scope and integrator all in one artifact.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe annual reports (CZ)
why_relevant: Vendor annual reports narrate CZ contract wins and segment revenue by client type — often naming banks that never appear in a case study. Historic PDFs give a longitudinal view of the CZ banking IT install base.

source_name: IBS Intelligence — core banking deal coverage (CZ)
why_relevant: Specialist banking-technology trade title that reports vendor selections independently and often adds contract context vendors omit; also runs sales-league tables that count CZ deals.

source_name: Shoptet Blog – Platební metody a platební brány (annual overview)
why_relevant: Vendor-neutral-ish annual roundup written for merchants, comparing CZ gateways, pricing models and feature sets; useful for tracking which providers the platform itself promotes and how the competitive set shifts year over year.

source_name: Alza.cz newsroom – Adyen partnership announcement
why_relevant: Primary confirmation that the largest Czech e-tailer switched its online AND in-store terminal acquiring to Adyen, unifying providers across all countries it operates in. This is exactly the buy-side switch signal the cell targets, and implies displacement of an incumbent CZ acquirer.

source_name: Businesswire press release — Komerční banka selects Temenos (Jan 2021)
why_relevant: Wire-distributed vendor announcement establishes the contract award date for the largest CZ core-banking replacement. Wire services are the canonical vendor-win channel and are archived.

source_name: FinTech Futures / Banking Technology — Czech bank vendor selections (EN cross-check)
why_relevant: English trade press names the vendor and the deal scope for CZ bank selections (e.g. ČSOB choosing nCino for commercial lending); serves as the corroboration layer for Czech-language reporting and catches vendor-side announcements that CZ media skip.

source_name: Ackee — References (J&T Banka mobile banking)
why_relevant: Digital product studio delivering mobile banking for J&T Banka, with detail on security regime (OWASP MASVS testing, penetration tests). Shows which banks outsource mobile app builds to boutiques rather than to core integrators — a distinct procurement channel.

source_name: Adyen Knowledge Hub – Czech merchant case studies (Alza)
why_relevant: Supplier-published but merchant-validated case study describing why a major Czech merchant consolidated online + POS acquiring; template for finding equivalent case studies from other PSPs (Comgate, GoPay, Global Payments, Worldline, Nexi) targeting CZ merchants.

entity_name: Czech SI/consultancy case-study pages naming bank clients
source_name: Czech SI/consultancy case-study pages naming bank clients (Enehano, LLP CRM, eppTec)
why_relevant: Local implementation partners publish cs-language 'případové studie' naming the bank and the platform (Česká spořitelna/Salesforce — described as the largest CEE Salesforce implementation; Raiffeisenbank/Microsoft Dynamics CRM). These fill the gap where global vendors stay silent about CZ.

source_name: Euronet ATMs corporate press page (euronetatms.com)
why_relevant: Euronet's independent-ATM-deployer arm publishes CZ-market-specific statements (e.g. rebutting claims in the Czech market), revealing regulatory/PR friction and its CZ market posture rather than client wins.

source_name: Glassdoor – Diebold Nixdorf Czech Republic / Prague pages
why_relevant: Confirms Diebold Nixdorf's CZ engineering/service footprint (Prague and Plzeň) and surfaces role descriptions naming ATM software platforms (Vynamic/Vista) — direct evidence of who services CZ self-service fleets, corroborating the ČSOB self-service partnership.

source_name: Kiosk Marketplace — Czech self-service/branch automation coverage
why_relevant: Sister trade title carrying the same vendor releases with different headlines/metadata; useful redundancy and occasionally adds device counts and branch-format detail.

source_name: The Fintech Times — Czech fintech landscape features (EN)
why_relevant: Periodic country landscape write-ups that name active CZ players, regulators and recent deals — a fast orientation and actor-map refresher for the cell, to be verified against cs primary reporting.
